title: Fourier sums grouped by degree
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$. For each $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $\widehat f(S)$ be the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$, and let $W_k[f]$ be its Fourier weight at level $k$. Then $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}g(|S|)\widehat f(S)^2=\sum_{k=0}^{n}g(k)W_k[f]$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number
$g$ is a real-valued function on the natural numbers
$f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
For every $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$,
\[
 \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}g(|S|)\widehat f(S)^2
 =\sum_{k=0}^n g(k)W_k(f).
\]
